title: Automatic Adaptive Algorithm for Delineation of Cerebral-Spinal Fluid Regions in Mice
author: Ryszard S. Gomolka
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Save acquired images in NIfTI format.

To correct for intensity inhomogeneities coming from the B0 field and the profile of the Tx/Rx coil (in original method surface profile of the CryoProbe [34]), perform N4 bias field correction in the brain-extracted parenchyma using FAST tool in FSL (0.5 sigma, 20 mm FWHM, 4 iterations).

steps.title: Perform mouse brain MRI
steps.instruction: Acquire mouse brain images on a 9.4 T Bruker BioSpec (BioSpec 94/30 USR) equipped with a 240 mT/m gradient coil (BGA‑12S) and a cryogenically cooled Tx/Rx quadrature CryoProbe. Use a T2‑weighted 2D RARE sequence for spatial planning and acquire two orthogonal 3D‑TrueFISP volumes (phase‑encoding 0° and 180°) for CSF space imaging. Refer to the original paper for full sequence parameters.

steps.title: Install MATLAB and toolboxes
steps.instruction: Install MATLAB (Windows OS) from MathWorks and add the Image Processing Toolbox (functions: niftiread, bwboundaries, medfilt3, permute, imshow) and the Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox (function: prctile).

steps.title: Acquire 3D‑TrueFISP volumes
steps.instruction: Collect two 3D‑TrueFISP volumes of the mouse brain, one with phase‑encoding direction 0° and the other with 180°.

steps.title: Save images as NIfTI
steps.instruction: Export the acquired 3D‑TrueFISP datasets to NIfTI format files.

steps.title: Create 3D‑CISS image
steps.instruction: Generate a 3D‑CISS image from the two 3D‑TrueFISP volumes:

substeps.instruction: a. Motion‑correct each 3D‑TrueFISP volume (if multiple repetitions were acquired) using AFNI’s 3Dvolreg() up to 10 iterations or until no further improvement.
b. Average all repetitions for each phase‑encoding direction.
c. Rigid‑body register the 180° averaged volume to the 0° averaged volume (6 d.f., AFNI 3Dvolreg()).
d. Compute a maximum‑intensity projection of the two co‑registered volumes to obtain the final 3D‑CISS image, which is largely free of banding artifacts.

steps.title: Segment brain parenchyma
steps.instruction: Perform semi‑automatic segmentation of the brain parenchyma on the 3D‑CISS image using the Segment 3D tool in ITK‑SNAP (or any equivalent semi‑automatic/automatic method). Include the tissue surrounded by the skull and intracerebral vessels as defined in the reference.

steps.title: Correct intensity bias
steps.instruction: Run N4 bias‑field correction on the brain‑extracted 3D‑CISS volume with FSL’s FAST tool using parameters: 0.5 sigma, 20 mm FWHM, 4 iterations.

steps.title: Run CSF segmentation algorithm
steps.instruction: Execute the adaptive CSF‑space segmentation in MATLAB (CSF_volumetry() or CSF_volumetry_gui()). The pipeline consists of the following sub‑steps:

substeps.instruction: 1. Compute brain bounding box and discard high‑intensity voxels not adjacent to the parenchyma. Remove isolated regions whose slice‑wise geometry satisfies eccentricity ≥ 0.5, roundness ≥ 0.5, and perimeter ≥ 4. Apply percentile thresholds based on image SNR:
• SNR > 4: P = 95.5 + xp (xp limited so P stays between 92 % and 97 %).
• SNR ≤ 2: P = 95.5 − xp (again limited to 92‑97 %).
2. Enhance CSF seed regions (intensify_CSF):
a. Flatten the bias‑corrected brain image to a vector, compute mean (µ_vect) and standard deviation (σ_vect) of non‑zero voxels.
b. Normalize each voxel: image_norm = (image − 1.33 × σ_vect) / σ_vect.
c. Determine the intensity at the P‑percentile (Px) of the positive‑intensity distribution; set voxels ≤ Px to 0.
d. Binarize remaining voxels (1 = CSF seed).
e. OPTIONAL: Apply a 3‑D median filter (3 × 3 × 3 kernel) to the binary mask if low SNR produces spurious fragments.
3. Region growing in sagittal plane (grow_regions):
a. Dilation: keep voxels with intensity ≥ (97.5 th − xp) percentile (≈ µ_d + 2 σ_d) and with absolute relative contrast to the boundary ≤ α = 2 %.
b. Erosion: remove voxels with intensity ≤ (95.5 th − xp) percentile and contrast > α2 = 2.5 %.

4. Region growing in axial and coronal planes (grow_regions2): repeat the dilation/erosion steps using the same percentile limits, with contrast evaluated over n = 1‑3 voxels (axial/coronal) and n = 1‑4 voxels (sagittal).
a. OPTIONAL: Apply a 2‑D median filter (3 × 3 kernel) to each slice after this step if required.
5. Save final masks:
• Save the unfiltered mask as <original_name>_CSF_mask_final.nii.
• If median filtering was used, also save <original_name>_CSF_mask_medfilt_final.nii.
• Both files are written in NIfTI format to the same directory as the input image.

steps.title: Verify completion
steps.instruction: After the algorithm finishes, a confirmation dialog appears. Optionally note that on a PC with an Intel Core i7‑10700U (6‑core) and 32 GB RAM, processing a whole‑brain 3D‑CISS image (33 µm isotropic voxels) takes ~3.5–4.5 min.
